reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses eutectic high-entropy alloys with fcc+B2 microstructures and strengthening mechanisms, not the single-phase BCC HfMoTaTiZr system. No specific prior evidence is provided to support the key premises about Hf and Ti's roles in density reduction, BCC phase stability, or high-temperature strength retention in this alloy.
premises: Hf is a heavy element that substantially contributes to density in HfMoTaTiZr
Ti is a lighter element that can maintain the BCC structure and solid-solution strengthening
Partial substitution of Hf with Ti reduces average atomic mass and thus density
The modified alloy retains a single-phase BCC microstructure with preserved lattice distortion
Retained BCC structure and solid-solution strengthening ensure comparable strength at room temperature and ~1000 °C
